Read docs/issues/ISS-0048.yaml in full for the original finding. Root cause task: find which test helper(s)/call site(s) provision a tenant Postgres schema (via Letflow.TenantProvisioning.provision_tenant_schema/1, replay_migrations/2, or similar) WITHOUT a matching on_exit DROP SCHEMA cleanup step, across test/letflow/identity_test.exs, test/letflow/identity/user_test.exs, test/letflow/identity/group_test.exs, test/letflow/identity/tenant_role_test.exs, test/letflow/role_registry_test.exs, and any shared test/support helper they call into. You have Postgres access via the running docker compose stack in this checkout (~/letflow) -- config/test.exs points at localhost:5462; do NOT run docker compose up (already running), and do not touch ~/letflow-wt2. Independently reproduce/confirm the orphaned-schema population is real (e.g. `docker exec letflow-postgres-1 psql -U postgres -d letflow_test -c "SELECT schema_name FROM information_schema.schemata WHERE schema_name ~ '^(tenant_|sandbox_)' AND schema_name NOT IN (SELECT schema_name FROM tenant_schemas)"` or the equivalent against whatever the actual test DB name is -- check config/test.exs) rather than trusting the original finding's prose alone (No Speculation). Grep every provision_tenant_schema/replay_migrations call site under test/ and check each has a corresponding on_exit cleanup (DROP SCHEMA or an existing sandbox-teardown helper).
acceptance_criteria: Root cause identified and written into result.summary: the specific call site(s) (file:line) missing on_exit cleanup, or confirmation that a different mechanism (e.g. a crash/interrupt path) is the actual cause
Orphaned-schema population independently reproduced/confirmed via a live Postgres query against the shared test database, not just cited from the original ISS-0048.yaml text
Diagnosis states what a fix needs to change (e.g. add on_exit cleanup to specific test modules/helpers, or a shared ExUnit case template fix) -- does NOT implement the fix itself
Does not touch or modify any other checkout (~/letflow-wt2) or run docker compose up in this checkout

result.summary:
STEP 0.5 (registry lookup): grepped docs/issues/*.yaml for status: resolved entries mentioning schema/provisioning/tenant_schemas symptoms -- ISS-0027 (missing validate_format on Registration.schema_name, unrelated -- DDL-injection hardening, not cleanup) and ISS-0005 (stale R-Co design docs, unrelated) are the only textual hits besides ISS-0048 itself; ISS-0050 (order-dependent DropLegacyPublicIdentityTables full-suite flake) explicitly self-references ISS-0048 as 'likely the same general class' but is a distinct symptom (a migration-guard failure under full-suite concurrency, not schema accumulation) and is not resolved/closed as a duplicate. No true prior-resolved match found -- this is not a recurrence.

STEP 1 (diagnose): Live-reproduced against the actual running container (docker exec letflow-postgres-1, Up continuously since 2026-08-17T08:16Z per `docker inspect`, i.e. the SAME container TEST-DESIGN-VALIDATOR queried at discovery time on 2026-08-18 -- not restarted since). Credentials are username/password 'letflow' (config/test.exs), not 'postgres' as the handoff's suggested query assumed -- corrected. Checked all three live test-partition databases (letflow_test, letflow_test2, letflow_test99, per MIX_TEST_PARTITION -- `\l` on the postgres container). Result: letflow_test has 1 orphaned schema (sandbox_5050499590a9426186656f72f7296622, confirmed via NOT EXISTS against public.tenant_schemas, which currently has 0 rows); letflow_test2 and letflow_test99 have 0. tenant_* schema count across all three DBs is 0.

This is a materially different population than ISS-0048/GAP-ORPHANED-SCHEMAS's own citation: TEST-DESIGN-VALIDATOR independently re-confirmed 69 orphaned tenant_*/sandbox_* schemas in this exact container/database twice (pre- and post- full-suite run) on 2026-08-18 ~12:11-12:16Z (handoffs/WF02-REQ063-20260818/step-03b-test-design-gate.json). I could not reproduce that count now (~10h later, same non-restarted container) -- the tenant_* population is entirely gone (0), with no docker restart/volume-recreate in between (`docker inspect .State.StartedAt` predates discovery) and no commit/handoff evidence of a bulk cleanup script or `mix ecto.reset` run in the intervening git log (checked `git log --since/--until` across that window and grepped handoffs/ for ecto.reset/ecto.drop -- none found). This gap is itself worth flagging to CODE-DESIGNER/ORCH as unexplained, not just noted.

Given the live population no longer supports the original 5-file hypothesis, I verified that hypothesis directly rather than trusting it: read test/letflow/identity_test.exs (provisioned_tenant!/1, ~line 141), test/letflow/identity/user_test.exs (point_search_path_at!/1, ~line 118), test/letflow/identity/group_test.exs (~line 53), test/letflow/identity/tenant_role_test.exs (~line 51), and test/letflow/role_registry_test.exs (~line 112) in full. All five register `on_exit(fn -> ... DROP SCHEMA IF EXISTS "#{schema_name}" CASCADE ... end)` BEFORE calling TenantProvisioning.provision_tenant_schema/1 or replay_migrations/2 (i.e. before the risky, potentially-raising calls) -- so even if provisioning raises, on_exit is already registered and will still fire the DROP SCHEMA. No missing on_exit gap found in any of the five files' happy or exception paths. ISS-0048's own 'likely candidates' text was speculative prose per WF-03's Step 1 mandate against diagnosing from prose alone, and it does not hold up under direct reading -- these five files are not confirmed to be a current or recent leak source.

The ONE orphan schema that IS live and reproducible right now belongs to a structurally different, genuinely-demonstrated mechanism: Letflow.SandboxPool (lib/letflow/sandbox_pool.ex), a separate ephemeral-schema pool used by Letflow.Definitions.apply_promotion_assertion_rerun/6 (lib/letflow/definitions.ex ~line 1780-1820) for promotion-assertion replay sandboxes. Two compounding facts: (1) sandbox_* schemas are BY DESIGN never registered in public.tenant_schemas (lib/letflow/sandbox_pool.ex:239-243's own comment: 'registry-coupled... inappropriate for an ephemeral, non-tenant sandbox schema') -- so ISS-0048's own detection query (schema NOT IN tenant_schemas) will flag every sandbox_* schema as 'orphaned' even when correctly mid-lifecycle, which is a methodology caveat CODE-DESIGNER should know about, not just a cleanup gap; (2) apply_promotion_assertion_rerun/6's own moduledoc (lib/letflow/definitions.ex ~1809-1813) explicitly discloses: 'the claim-through-release span is wrapped in try/rescue... It does NOT cover a hard process kill or a BEAM crash mid-replay -- that residual gap is disclosed, not resolved, and left to a deferred reaper follow-up.' Grepped lib/ for 'reaper' -- zero implementation hits, only design-doc mentions (lib/letflow/design/req040-promotion-assertion-rerun.md) -- confirmed this reaper was never built. `try/rescue` in Elixir does not catch `exit` signals (process kills, linked-process crash propagation, ExUnit test-timeout kills), only raised exceptions -- so any test or production path that kills the owning process between SandboxPool.claim/2 and release/2 (or GenServer.stop of the pool itself before release) leaks the claimed schema exactly once per such event, with no safety net. I read test/letflow/definitions/promotion_assertion_rerun_test.exs's 'try/rescue crash safety' describe block (line 824+) directly and confirmed its one crash test (raising evaluator) IS a rescued raise, not a real kill, and DOES assert no leak (`refute schema_exists?(...)`) -- so this specific test is not the source of the one live orphan; the orphan is consistent with some other, unlogged past test/dev-session process kill (e.g. an interrupted `mix test` run, Ctrl-C, or ExUnit timeout) against this same long-lived container, for which there is genuinely no code-level protection today.

What a fix needs to change (routing to CODE-DESIGNER): (a) primary, confirmed-reproducible target -- give Letflow.SandboxPool-owning callers (apply_promotion_assertion_rerun/6 at minimum) a real safety net for the exit/kill case the moduledoc already discloses as unresolved: either a supervised claim-owner-monitor inside SandboxPool itself that DROP SCHEMAs a claim when its owning process dies (mirrors DBConnection.Ownership.Manager's own :DOWN-monitor reclaim pattern, already proven elsewhere in this codebase per test/support/data_case.ex), or a standalone periodic reaper task comparing pg_namespace sandbox_*/tenant_* schemas against tenant_schemas + an active-claims table and dropping true orphans past some age threshold; (b) do NOT change the 5 originally-named identity/role_registry test files -- direct reading found no gap in their on_exit ordering, and the current live evidence does not implicate them; (c) before designing further, CODE-DESIGNER (or ORCH) should re-run this same live query after a few more full-suite passes to see whether the tenant_* class re-accumulates at all under current code, since it could not be reproduced in this session -- if it stays at 0, the tenant_* half of ISS-0048's original title may already be moot and only the sandbox_*/SandboxPool crash-safety gap remains real and actionable.
